title: HTTP requests from browser and Node
summary: Make HTTP requests from browser and Node with interceptors, global configuration, mocking and cookie handling. Monitor axios and the packages commonly pulled in by other application libraries, such as Firebase, for maintenance, advisories, duplication and unnecessary packages, and compare the role of each candidate with native fetch.
constraints: Actively maintained and responsive to security reports
No unfixed high or critical advisories
Works in both browser and Node environments
Compatible with the existing axios interceptors, global config and mocking approach
Permissive license across the full dependency tree
No install scripts in the dependency tree
Avoid duplicate or unnecessary direct dependencies; treat an unverified parent chain as context, not proof of use
If npm provenance is unavailable, pin exact versions and record the gap
out_of_scope: Detailed performance benchmark against every HTTP client
notes: This is a mixed monitoring batch: axios, follow-redirects, undici, fast-uri, js-cookie, protobufjs and cookie. Only axios -> follow-redirects is a verified edge in the collected dossiers. The requester reports that the other five are pulled in by other libraries such as Firebase; walk those parent chains before treating them as verified members. The candidates have different roles; compare each package's purpose, maintenance, advisories, licence, install scripts and overlap with the rest of the stack rather than treating them as interchangeable HTTP clients. Native fetch is the considered alternative, but it is not a candidate in this batch.
